what: Vanilla Snake's DOWN THROW (ThrowLw) on the live pgwr G&W body, eflame c06/c07, replacing G&W's own down throw on those costumes only

move_identity.why: Snake's own motion_list.bin gives throw_lw the game script game_throwlw and the clip e01throwlw.nuanmb (cancel 48), while attack_lw4 gets game_attacklw4 and c04attacklw4.nuanmb (cancel 56). attack_data_param.prc lists an attack_lw4 AI record at cancel_frame 56 and NO throw_lw record, and game_attacklw4 opens with START_SMASH_HOLD, se_common_smash_start_02, rbkind_smashhold1 and PHYSICS_START_CHARGE with an AttackLw4Charge follow-up clip. Those are down-SMASH marks. Measured by tools/audit_snake_throw_lw_donor.py, recorded in inventory.json, with a negative control asserting the two kinds' game scripts differ.

acmd_text.kind: third-party decompiled text at a pinned commit
acmd_text.why_this_commit: the commit refs/brave_special_n/acmd_pin.json and tools/fetch_donor_acmd.py already pin, and the one refs/snake_attack_hi3/donor_acmd used on 2026-10-02; dumps/scripts/SSBU-Dumped-Scripts-main is no longer in this workspace

arc.kind: offline extraction from the local base game, read-only
arc.note: Base-game files only. Extracted into gamedata/ and pinned into refs/; nothing was written into dump/ or a source tree.

files_whose_names_look_related.e01throwlw.nuanmb: the ATTACKER's own down-throw clip - the one this port retargets
files_whose_names_look_related.e01thrownlw.nuanmb: a SNAKE being thrown by a down throw - i.e. Snake as the VICTIM
files_whose_names_look_related.e01throwndxlw.nuanmb: the same victim, the down-throw variant

victim_anatomy.why_the_victim_clips_are_not_ported: They live under the VICTIM's own fighter folder in the base game. Whoever is grabbed plays their own e01thrownlw from their own files, so the victim-side animation is already vanilla-correct for every opponent and is not this mod's to ship. Copying Snake's would only change what a Snake victim looks like, and Snake is not a roster member of this mod.
victim_anatomy.progression: throw (capture) -> throw (held) -> released at the donor's frame 35 -> the victim's own THROWN/DAMAGE state -> LAY_DOWN -> the victim's own get-up.

bones.measured_on_built_recipient: absent (165-bone c06/c07 skeleton). 'throw' is an engine fighter anchor of the same family as 'top', not a skeleton bone, and G&W's own down throw - what runs on c06/c07 today - names the same anchor. Left exactly as the donor wrote it, measured rather than assumed.

dependencies.articles: none - the donor's game_throwlw writes no work id and generates no article
dependencies.effects: NONE. Snake's ThrowLw defines no effect script, so no effect bank is merged and no config.json entry is needed. G&W's four down-throw effects are superseded by a deliberately empty effect_throwlw at High priority - see the module docs.

sounds.why: se_snake_catch_tight is the only KIND-1 (sequence) tone among the 111 tones of se_snake_c00 and references its two children by bank-relative index 92/93. Appending it without them, or without rebasing the indices, would point at two unrelated tones in Pyra's 544-tone bank while every byte-level check still passed.
sounds.sequences: none - the donor plays no PLAY_SEQUENCE, so eflame.sqb is deliberately not written

dependencies.params: Snake's vl.prc was decoded and carries no throw_lw entry (hit_data is 11 limb capsules, hit_target is [0,1]); attack_data_param.prc carries no throw_lw record. The move is inline ACMD plus its motion-list entry. attack_list_param.prc is pinned for completeness and is not used.
dependencies.statuses: NONE. ThrowLw is a vanilla status kind entered from the grab, so this move allocates NO custom status id and requests none from the collective pool. Next free Pyra id remains 0x208.

victim_outcome_analysis.question: is this a damage number plus a downward launch?
victim_outcome_analysis.answer: No, and the donor's numbers are the evidence.
victim_outcome_analysis.measured: The throw's ATTACK_ABS is damage 9.0, angle 270, and kbg / fkb / bkb ALL ZERO. There is no knockback to copy, so the numbers alone cannot produce the move's behaviour.
victim_outcome_analysis.actual_mechanism: collision_attr_lay on the throw box is what routes the victim into the engine's generic prone state FIGHTER_STATUS_KIND_LAY_DOWN (0x56 in the pinned lua_const.rs) rather than the DAMAGE_FLY* family. The victim lying down and standing back up is then run by the victim's own fighter.
victim_outcome_analysis.why_this_matters_for_the_port: Replacing the two ATTACK_ABS calls with a plain downward launch, or dropping the lay attribute, would keep the damage number and still be a different move. All three pieces are carried verbatim: the CATCH box (damage 2.0, angle 361, kbg 100, fkb 60, ATTACK_LR_CHECK_B), the release (ATK_HIT_ABS on bone 'throw' at frame 35, reading the three THROW work ids), and the lay attribute.
victim_outcome_analysis.tier: B for the numbers and the attribute (read from pinned vanilla text and the pinned const table); D for the observed victim animation and get-up timing, which only the console can show.

not_established: how the move looks on G&W's body
whether the victim is actually released (the 'throw' anchor is not on the built skeleton)
whether the victim visibly lies prone and how long the get-up takes
whether the two Snake tones play, and whether the sequence tone resolves
whether the four G&W down-throw effects are indeed silent

verification.hardware: none. No console, no emulator, no card access, no automated gameplay test.
